summary: Dock-induced USB HID re-enumeration breaks Windows Hello fingerprint enrollment during provisioning on Dell Precision 7770
description:
Issue summary: Multiple provisioning jobs for docked Dell Precision 7770 machines fail to complete Windows Hello fingerprint enrollment during post-image OOBE. Machines enter a provisioning loop where Hello enrollment step times out and Autopilot task retries.

Impact: Blocks new-hire provisioning and re-provisioning after depot repairs for ~18 machines across two regions. End users cannot finish account setup without IT intervention.

Environment: corp prod Autopilot + Intune autopilot profile, BitLocker enabled, VBS enabled, Hello for Business configured with TPM attestation. Affected devices observed primarily when dock firmware recently updated (WD19TBS series) and device was docked during first boot.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Attach Dell Precision 7770 to WD19TBS dock with recent firmware (firmware v1.2.4 -> v1.3.0 applied by depot).
2. Boot to Autopilot OOBE with corporate image.
3. Let Intune apply enrollment policies and Windows Hello for Business configuration.
4. When prompted to enroll fingerprint, the system shows spinner and then times out; provisioning task retries and OOBE loops back to earlier screen.

Observed behavior: Fingerprint reader is present but Windows reports "Device needs setup" and Event Viewer records multiple Instance ID changes for the fingerprint HID device. Credential Manager shows missing PIN/biometric providers after retries. If user undocks, fingerprint device reappears with a different device instance path and enrollment succeeds.

Expected behavior: Docked or undocked machines should present the same device instance path for fingerprint sensor and allow Hello enrollment during OOBE without manual undock.

Logs / evidence:
- EVTX excerpts: "Kernel-PnP: Device instance path changed: USB\\VID_27C6&PID_5501\\6&3a7d9f5b&0&0000 -> USB\\VID_27C6&PID_5501\\6&3a7d9f5b&0&0001"
- Intune MDM logs: "HelloProvisioningTimeout" with 0x8007007e after 15m
- Support screenshots uploaded to ticket (attachment IDs in comment).
- Slack thread: #support channel link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05XXXXXX/p1676839200000
investigation_notes: 2026-02-25 Priya: Triage - reproduced with dock firmware v1.3.0 in our us-west lab; undocking allows enrollment to continue. Imaging team notified.

2026-02-26 Ethan: Captured PnP Event IDs showing device instance path increment (0000 -> 0001) mid-OOBE when dock present. Hypothesis: Dock firmware update changes USB hub topology on initial enumeration causing Windows to perceive a new device instance.

2026-02-26 SRE (Miguel): Verified we see identical behavior when VBS is enabled and Hello uses TPM attestation - TPM still works but Hello provider ties biometric registration to device instance path; re-enumeration invalidates registration flow.

2026-02-27 Hardware vendor (Dell) response: Confirmed a change in composite device descriptor in firmware v1.3.0 that can trigger a re-enumeration on first host attach. They provided a firmware hotfix candidate and internal notes linking to FR-99831.

2026-02-28 Engineering (Kunal): Tested vendor hotfix (dock_firmware_1.3.1_rc) in lab; re-enumeration no longer observed. Created automation script to clear stale PnP device instances during provisioning as interim mitigation (see PR).
comments: 2026-02-25 09:12 Priya Nair: Created ticket after escalations from Desk Ops. Initial batch of affected devices: 12 in us-west, 6 in eu-west. Assigning to Ethan for triage.

2026-02-26 10:04 Ethan Kim: Reproduced in lab with dock firmware v1.3.0. Attaching PnP logs and Intune MDM traces. Suspect dock firmware changed composite descriptor causing HID to reattach under a new instance path during OOBE.
2026-02-26 14:30 Dell Support: We see an internal change in 1.3.0 that can cause re-enumeration on first attach. Patch scheduled; will provide RC build for validation.

2026-02-27 16:20 Miguel (SRE): Confirmed repro matrix when VBS enabled and Hello for Business forced via policy. Workaround confirmed: undock before Hello step or disable Hello via policy until post-enrollment device restart.

2026-03-01 11:05 Kunal (Eng): Deployed automation script in corp-imaging repository to run 'pnputil /remove-device' for orphaned instances during OOBE; raising PR for code review: github.com/redwood-inference/it-scripts/pull/412.

2026-03-02 09:40 Priya Nair: Dell released firmware v1.3.1 to depot; redeployed to affected machines. Verified three previously blocked devices completed provisioning end-to-end. Marking as resolved and documenting follow-up.

2026-03-02 10:05 Ethan Kim: Closing note - created Confluence runbook for desk agents: steps to undock, clear biometric device instance, and reattempt enrollment. Link added to related_confluence_pages.
resolution: Workaround and permanent fix applied. Short-term mitigation: instruct depot and desk agents to undock devices during OOBE or run the supplied pnputil script to remove stale HID instances before Hello enrollment. Long-term fix: vendor firmware hotfix v1.3.1 rolled out to WD19TBS fleet; imaging pipeline updated to include a check that fails provisioning if dock firmware < 1.3.1 with automated remediation. Automation PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/it-scripts/pull/412. Post-deploy verification completed for sampled devices in us-west and eu-west.
follow_up_tasks: Add dock firmware version gating to depot workflow (owner: Hardware Ops)
Add automated pnputil cleanup step to Autopilot OOBE imaging task (owner: Imaging)
Update device onboarding KB for Desk Ops with undock guidance and Confluence runbook link (owner: IT Support)
Monitor Intune enrollment success rate for 2 weeks and report regressions (owner: SRE)
Open vendor FR follow-up with Dell for permanent enumeration stability fix (vendor ticket FR-99831)
